_variant_note: Wave-5 Goldilocks derive-args chain: get_all_requests → get_request_status. Customer asks about 'my card application from last month.' NOISE (REQ-SO-95001, listed FIRST, raised 2026-07-25) has description 'New card issuance processed via branch' — semantic overlap ('card issuance' ≈ 'card application') without literal keyword match — and category = 'cheque_book'. CORRECT (REQ-SO-95002, listed SECOND, raised 2026-07-08) has description 'Debit card replacement — dispatch pending', category = 'other'. The noise has card semantics but wrong category — a small model should map 'card issuance' to 'card application' and pick the noise. a strong model should notice the category mismatch and pick the correct one.

gold.expected_resolution: Customer asks about the status of 'a card application from last month.' get_all_requests shows REQ-SO-95001 (cheque_book, raised 2026-07-25, 'New card issuance processed via branch') and REQ-SO-95002 (other, raised 2026-07-08, 'Debit card replacement — dispatch pending'). The noise (REQ-SO-95001) semantically overlaps with 'card application' ('card issuance' ≈ 'card application') without containing the exact keyword — a weak model would map them. However the REAL request is REQ-SO-95002 (debit card replacement). The noise category (cheque_book) is mismatched. The assistant must identify REQ-SO-95002 and report its status: in progress, card dispatched via courier, expected delivery in 3-5 business days. Checking REQ-SO-95001 fails.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: correctly identifies REQ-SO-95002 (debit card replacement, in_progress) as the relevant request and reports its status: replacement card dispatched via courier, expected delivery in 3-5 business days. Picking REQ-SO-95001 (cheque_book category, 'New card issuance') despite its semantic overlap with the customer's phrasing fails.
